In the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon, I'm auditing the background worker process (everything under worker/) for code that assumes there's only ONE physical Proxmox compute node, now that the platform has two (primary: OVH Singapore; node-2: Hetzner Falkenstein — `Node` Prisma model in schema.prisma, one row per physical host, each with its own `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret`/`publicIp`/`natChain`/`subnetPrefix`).

I already found and CONFIRMED one bug in this area, already documented — do not re-report it, just note it for context: `worker/network.ts`'s `syncPortForwards()` queries ALL servers platform-wide with no `nodeId` filter, and reconciles them against ONE local iptables chain (`process.env.NXEON_NAT_CHAIN ?? "NXEON_FWD"`) via direct `execFile("iptables", ...)` calls — this only ever touches the iptables of whatever machine the worker process itself is physically running on (the primary), so it can never create/maintain NAT rules on a second node's own iptables. This is a known, confirmed gap (tracked as P1-18 in docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md already — read that file for the existing writeup if useful context).

Your job: audit EVERY OTHER file in worker/ (index.ts, monitor.ts, billing.ts, backups.ts — check what files actually exist first) for the SAME CLASS of bug: any sweep/job/cron-style loop that:
(a) queries the DB for a global list of servers/resources WITHOUT filtering or grouping by `nodeId`, when it then needs to reach out to something that lives on a SPECIFIC physical node (local filesystem paths, local commands like `iptables`/`zfs`/`qm`, a bare Proxmox singleton call, an SSH connection, a local socket, etc.)
(b) assumes "the node" is singular anywhere (a comment, a variable name, a hardcoded path like `/tank/backup` or `/var/lib/vz` used without first confirming which node's storage that even is)
(c) is scoped correctly already (loops `db.node.findMany()` and dispatches per-node, e.g. via `pveForNode`) — note these as confirmed-safe so I know what NOT to touch

Specifically check: the periodic dedicated-IP pool sync (I already know this one loops over all nodes correctly, from earlier work today — confirm it's still fine, don't deep-dive), backup pruning/retention sweeps, snapshot sweeps, health/monitoring sweeps (worker-side, not the admin dashboard reads I already redesigned today), any DNS sync jobs, any node-capacity-alert sweep (`nodeCapacitySweep` — check if it's already correctly per-node via `proxmoxNodeUtil()`), template/OS-image sync jobs if any, and the game-server auto-update sweep. For each worker file, give a one-paragraph summary of what it does and whether it's single-node-assumption-bugged or already correctly multi-node.

Also check: is there exactly ONE worker process for the whole platform (i.e., does `nxeon-worker` run only on the primary machine, with no equivalent process on node-2)? If so, that's the root architectural reason ANY worker job doing host-local execution for node-2 can never work without either (a) worker-to-node remote execution (SSH or an API), or (b) a second worker-like process running ON node-2 itself. Note which specific jobs would need which category of fix.

This is a research task only — do not write or edit any files. Report organized by file, ending with a prioritized list (most customer-impact first) of which jobs have the bug and what class of fix each would need (remote-exec from primary vs. a local per-node agent). Keep it precise with file:line citations.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Nxeon — onboard a fresh Proxmox VE host as a compute node
# =============================================================================
# Run this ON the new Proxmox host (as root). It idempotently preps everything a
# Nxeon compute node needs, then prints the exact values to paste into the admin
# "Add node" form (/admin/nodes/new). Re-running is safe: every step checks
# current state before changing anything.
#
# What it does:
#   1. Create a NAT bridge vmbrX bound to a per-node /24 (e.g. 10.20.N.1/24)
#   2. Enable IPv4 forwarding + a MASQUERADE rule for that subnet (append-only)
#   3. Create the NVMe + HDD storages matching the Node's storageNvme/storageHdd
#   4. Create the cloud-init snippets dir + the nxeon vendor snippet
#   5. Create a Proxmox API role + user + token with the privileges the platform
#      needs (documented pveum commands)
#   6. Build (or document copying) the cloud-init templates VMID 9000-9004
#   7. Print the Add-node form values (apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, pveNode,
#      subnetPrefix, natChain, sshPort range, storages, publicIp)
#
# SAFETY:
#   - Never flushes the firewall. It only APPENDS its own MASQUERADE/FORWARD
#     rules and only if an identical rule is not already present.
#   - Never touches running VMs. Template builds skip any VMID that exists.
#   - Never destroys storage. `pvesm add` is skipped when the storage id exists.
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CROSS-HOST NETWORKING — IMPORTANT LIMITATION (read before deploying node #2)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each node NATs its OWN private /24 (10.20.N.0/24) behind its OWN public IP.
# This makes each node fully self-sufficient for provisioning, IP allocation and
# SSH DNAT — but it does NOT give VMs on different physical hosts a shared LAN.
#
#   * A VM on node-1 (10.20.0.x) CANNOT reach a VM on node-2 (10.20.1.x) over the
#     private network. They are separate NAT islands.
#   * The worker's iptables NAT chain (NXEON_FWD*) is rebuilt per-host from the
#     DB; it only manages forwards local to the host it runs on.
#
# If you need private east-west connectivity between VMs on different nodes you
# must lay an overlay/VPN over the public IPs — e.g. WireGuard mesh or a VXLAN
# fabric (Proxmox SDN "VXLAN zone") — and route the /24s across it. That is out
# of scope for this script; it is a deliberate, documented follow-up. For the
# common case (independent single-node VPS customers) per-node NAT islands are
# exactly what you want.
#
# Assumption: node #2 is a SEPARATE physical box with its own public IP, NOT a
# second NIC on the same L2 as node #1. If two nodes truly share L2 you would
# instead give them the SAME bridge/subnet and split the IP range — but this
# script assumes the separate-host model above.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ---------- Parameters (flags override env) ----------------------------------
NODE_NUM="${NODE_NUM:-2}"           # ordinal; drives subnet + nat chain defaults
SUBNET_OCTET=""                     # third octet of 10.20.X.0/24 (default: NODE_NUM-1)
PUBLIC_IP="${PUBLIC_IP:-}"          # this host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if empty)
BRIDGE=""                           # vmbrX (default: vmbr1)
NVME_STORAGE="${NVME_STORAGE:-vmdata}"
HDD_STORAGE="${HDD_STORAGE:-vmdata-hdd}"
NVME_ZPOOL="${NVME_ZPOOL:-}"        # existing ZFS pool for NVMe storage (optional)
HDD_DIR="${HDD_DIR:-/tank/backup}"  # dir-backed HDD storage path
SNIPPETS_STORAGE="${SNIPPETS_STORAGE:-$HDD_STORAGE}"
TOKEN_USER="${TOKEN_USER:-nxeon@pve}"
TOKEN_NAME="${TOKEN_NAME:-platform}"
TOKEN_ROLE="${TOKEN_ROLE:-NxeonProvision}"
BUILD_TEMPLATES="${BUILD_TEMPLATES:-0}"   # 1 = build 9000-9004 here; 0 = document copying
SSH_PORT_START="${SSH_PORT_START:-20000}"
SSH_PORT_END="${SSH_PORT_END:-29999}"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [flags]
  --node-num N          Node ordinal (default 2). Sets defaults for subnet + nat chain.
  --subnet-octet N      Third octet of the /24 (default: node-num - 1, e.g. node 2 -> 1 -> 10.20.1.0/24).
  --public-ip IP        This host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if omitted).
  --bridge vmbrX        NAT bridge name (default vmbr1).
  --nvme-storage NAME   NVMe storage id (default vmdata).
  --hdd-storage NAME    HDD storage id (default vmdata-hdd).
  --nvme-zpool POOL     Existing ZFS pool to back the NVMe storage (zfspool). Optional.
  --hdd-dir PATH        Directory for the HDD (dir) storage (default /tank/backup).
  --build-templates     Build cloud-init templates 9000-9004 on this host.
  -h, --help            Show this help.

Environment variables mirror the flags (NODE_NUM, PUBLIC_IP, BRIDGE, ...).
EOF
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --node-num) NODE_NUM="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --subnet-octet) SUBNET_OCTET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --public-ip) PUBLIC_IP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --bridge) BRIDGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --nvme-storage) NVME_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --hdd-storage) HDD_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --nvme-zpool) NVME_ZPOOL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --hdd-dir) HDD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --build-templates) BUILD_TEMPLATES=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown flag: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).

# Multi-Node Single-Host Assumption Audit — `worker/` (excluding `worker/network.ts`, already confirmed as P1-18)

## 0. Architecture ground truth (needed before the file-by-file)

**There is exactly one worker process for the whole platform, and it runs only on the primary.**

- `package.json:9` — `"worker": "tsx worker/index.ts"` — a single entrypoint, no per-node variant.
- `CLAUDE.md:8` — *"Worker: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables)."* One systemd unit name, singular.
- `scripts/promote-production.sh:92-95` — deploy does `systemctl restart nxeon-worker` on the box the script runs on (the primary/app server) — there is no equivalent step for a second node.
- `scripts/onboard-node.sh` (the node-2 bring-up script) provisions Proxmox-host things (bridge, storages, cloud-init templates, API token) but contains **zero** `systemctl`/`.service`/`worker` steps to install a worker-like process on the new node. Its own header comment (`:30-46`) explicitly says: *"A VM on node-1 (10.20.0.x) CANNOT reach a VM on node-2 (10.20.1.x) over the private network. They are separate NAT islands... The worker's iptables NAT chain (NXEON_FWD*) is rebuilt per-host from the DB; it only manages forwards local to the host it runs on."* — i.e. the script's author already knew the worker is host-local and never built a second one.

So: **every** job/sweep in `worker/` that needs to touch something physically local to node-2 (its filesystem, its iptables, its private bridge) categorically cannot, no matter how the DB query is scoped — there is no process running there to do it. The only way to make node-2 work today is **remote-exec from the primary** (SSH/API to node-2, from the single existing worker). A second per-node agent is architecturally cleaner but doesn't exist and isn't stubbed anywhere.

---

## 1. Two new cross-cutting bugs (same class as P1-18, not yet documented)

These aren't sweeps themselves, but they are the shared root cause behind most of the individual-file bugs below, so I'm calling them out once instead of repeating the mechanism in every paragraph.

### 1a. `lib/sftp.ts:137-143` `connectionTarget()` — never resolves the server's own node's public IP

```
export function connectionTarget(server: SftpServer): { host: string; port: number } | null {
  const dedicated = !!server.dedicatedIp;
  const host = dedicated ? server.dedicatedIp!.address : process.env.PUBLIC_IP || "";
  const port = dedicated ? 22 : server.sshPort;
  ...
}
```
For any non-dedicated-IP server it always dials the single global `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` (the primary's own address), never `server.node.publicIp`. The `SftpServer` type (`lib/sftp.ts:35-41`) doesn't even carry a `node` field, so callers have no way to override it. This is used by `withServerSsh`/`withSftp`/`exec` (`lib/ssh-exec.ts:24,114,192-237` — the doc comment literally says *"Connection target ... derived exactly like lib/sftp"*), which is the shared plumbing for essentially every "SSH into the customer's guest to do X" feature in `worker/`.

Two other call sites in the repo already do this correctly by preferring `server.node?.publicIp`: `worker/index.ts:712,814` and `lib/server-deployed-email.ts:67`. `connectionTarget()` is the one place that fix never landed — everything built on top of it inherited the gap.

**Impact for node-2:** every affected job dials `<primary's public IP>:<node-2 server's sshPort>`. Ports are allocated from one global pool (`lib/ipam.ts:248-273` `pickFreePort` checks `db.server` with no `nodeId` filter, so no two servers anywhere share a port), so this doesn't cross-wire two different customers' VMs — it just times out / connects to nothing on the primary (or, once P1-18 is fixed on node-2's own chain, still fails because the primary has no route to `10.20.1.0/24` to relay through even if its own chain had a stray forward for it).

**Fix class:** pure code fix, no new infrastructure. The worker already has a normal internet path to node-2's public IP; it just needs to dial the right one. Thread `node: { select: { publicIp: true } }` into every query that builds a `SftpServer`, and change `connectionTarget` to `const host = dedicated ? ... : (server.node?.publicIp ?? process.env.PUBLIC_IP ?? "")`. This is the same one-line pattern already proven at `index.ts:712`.

### 1b. Direct-private-IP dial pattern — `firewall.ts`, `game-update.ts`, `claude.ts`

Three files bypass `connectionTarget` entirely and dial `server.ipAddress` (the guest's **private** `10.20.N.x` address) on port 22 directly, reasoning that the worker sits on the same bridge as the guest:

- `worker/claude.ts:85-86` — *"The worker reaches VMs directly on the private bridge (10.20.0.0/24), so we connect to the private IP on port 22."* — hardcodes node-1's own CIDR as if it were universal. Used by `sshExec` (`:77-104`), called from `claudeBuild` (`:159`) and elsewhere (`:218`).
- `worker/game-update.ts:20-21` — *"`gameUpdate` runs the per-family update over SSH against the server's private IP (the worker can reach vmbr1)"* — same assumption, `execFile("sshpass", [..., "root@${server.ipAddress}", ...])` at `:104-119`.
- `worker/firewall.ts:95-107` — same `sshpass ssh root@${server.ipAddress}` (no `-p`/port at all) pattern, no comment but identical mechanism.

**Impact for node-2:** this doesn't fail the way the NAT bug does (a rejected/misrouted packet) — the primary has **no route at all** to `10.20.1.0/24` (separate, non-meshed NAT island per `onboard-node.sh`'s own header), so these calls simply hang until their own `ConnectTimeout`/`timeout` fires.

**Fix class:** either (a) rewrite these three files onto the same public-IP+forwarded-port path the rest of the codebase uses (pure code fix, same cost as 1a, and removes an inconsistency that exists even today between "how the worker reaches a guest" implementations), or (b) build the overlay VPN/mesh between node bridges that `onboard-node.sh` already flags as a "deliberate, documented follow-up" — genuinely new network infrastructure, not just a code change.

---

## 2. File-by-file

### Provisioning core

**`worker/index.ts`** — Owns the job-type→handler map and the single serial `for(;;)` loop (job polling + all the sweep timers). Its Proxmox-facing code is the *good* pattern: `nodeFor(server)` (`:107-118`) resolves `server.node` and builds a `pveFor(...)` client per node, correctly falling back to the env-singleton only when zero `Node` rows exist at all (bootstrap case, not a live multi-node bug), and `provision()` (`:442`) correctly derives `storage`, `bridge`, `subnetPrefix`-based gateway, and dedicated-IP eligibility from `nodeRow` (`:477-480, 519-527, 646`). **However**, buried inside that same correctly-parameterized `provision()` is a real bug: the per-server cloud-init **vendor snippet is written with plain Node.js `fs/promises.writeFile`** to `SNIPPET_DIR` (`:405,616`) and referenced via `cicustom=vendor=${SNIPPET_STORAGE}:snippets/...` (`:406,637`) — both are bare `process.env` globals, not derived from `nodeRow` at all, and the write always lands on whatever machine the worker process itself is running on (the primary). For a VM provisioned on node-2, Proxmox on node-2 is told to use a vendor snippet that was only ever written to the *primary's* `/tank/backup/snippets`, not node-2's. `buildCloudInit()` (`:232-297`) is what's inside that file: Claude Code install, Docker, ClamAV, the game family's install script (wrapped as a systemd unit), the NxCloud install hook, and the telemetry-shipper install. None of that reaches node-2 guests. Because the base template image already ships qemu-guest-agent (baked in at template-build time per `onboard-node.sh:238`, not via this snippet), `waitForGuestAgent` (`:690`) still passes and the job still reports success — this is the exact silent-broken-VM failure mode the code's own comment at `:594-601` says was fixed for local write failures, reintroduced for cross-node ones. `unlink` at `:915` (server delete) is comparatively harmless — it just fails to clean up a file that was never meaningful for node-2 anyway. **Bugged** (new finding, not P1-18).

### Monitoring

**`worker/monitor.ts`** — Runs `monitorSweep()` (disk/RAM/stuck-jobs/worker-liveness/backup-staleness/node-capacity checks) plus `sampleServerDisks`/`sampleServerBandwidth`/`sampleHealthSweep` on the main loop's 10-minute tick. This file is the best-scoped one in the audit: `sampleServerDisks` (`:290-344`) and `sampleServerBandwidth` (`:447-560ish`) both do `db.server.findMany` with `node: { select: {...} } }` included per row and build `pveFor(...)` per server (`:322-329, 532-539`), falling back to the singleton only when a row's `node` relation is genuinely null. `nodeCapacitySweep` (`:128`) → `proxmoxNodeUtil()` (`lib/node-capacity.ts:147`) → `nodeTargets()` (`lib/monitoring.ts:73-99`) all correctly loop `db.node.findMany({where:{enabled:true}})` and dispatch a `pveFor` client per node — this is the dedicated-IP-pool-sibling pattern you already confirmed; re-confirmed here, no changes needed. One minor nuance worth knowing about: `backupSummary()` (`lib/monitoring.ts:191-215`) *does* loop every node via `nodeTargets()`, but it **merges** every node's backup listing into one combined `{count, newestCtime, oldestCtime}` before `monitorSweep`'s item 5 (`:797-810`) checks staleness — so if node-1's backups are fresh but node-2's have silently stopped, the global `newestCtime` still looks healthy and node-2 never alerts. Not the (a)/(b) bug pattern verbatim (it does visit every node), but it's the same root problem in spirit: a monitoring signal that used to mean "one node" now silently means "whichever node happens to be freshest." **Mostly safe / confirmed correct**, with that one aggregation caveat.

### Networking

**`worker/network.ts`** — Already confirmed (P1-18), not re-audited here.

**`worker/firewall.ts`** — Per-job (`syncFirewall(job)`, one `serverId`) handler that rebuilds a customer's inbound guest-side `NXEON_FW` iptables chain over SSH. Uses the direct-private-IP dial pattern (§1b) — `root@${server.ipAddress}` with no port (`:95-107`). **Bugged**, independent of the shared `lib/sftp.ts` root cause.

### Backup / restore / storage

**`worker/backup-schedule.ts`** — `scheduledBackupSweep()` (`:29-94`) queries `db.server.findMany` platform-wide with no `nodeId` filter, but it **only enqueues a `BACKUP_CREATE` job** — no host-local or SSH action happens in this file at all. The actual work happens in `backupCreate` inside `index.ts`, which goes through the correct `nodeFor(server)`/`pruneBackups(conn,...)` pattern. **Confirmed safe** — textbook example of pattern (c) (sweep just enqueues, execution is properly node-scoped elsewhere).

**`worker/restore.ts`** — `backupRestore(job)`, per-server. `nodeFor(server)` (`:56-80`) is a verbatim, correct mirror of `index.ts`'s pattern. Identity reassertion (`reapplyIdentity`, `:92+`) and password re-application go through the per-node Proxmox client/guest-agent API, not SSH — no guest connection needed at all. **Confirmed safe**.

**`worker/volumes.ts`** — Per-job (`VOLUME_CREATE/ATTACH/DETACH/DELETE`). `nodeFor(server)` (`:93-117`) correctly mirrors `index.ts` for every Proxmox API call (attach/detach/resize disk). But `loadVolume`'s own comment (`:67-68`) admits the guest-prep step needs `lib/sftp` `connectionTarget`, and `prepareGuestVolume`/`releaseGuestVolume` (`:596-603, 738-745`) both call `withServerSsh` — inheriting the §1a bug for the in-guest format/mount/unmount step. **Half-bugged**: Proxmox-side disk operations are node-correct; the guest-side format/mount (the part that actually makes an attached volume usable, and the part that safely unmounts before detach) is not.

**`worker/disk-expand.ts`** — Per-job (`diskExpand(job)`, `:283`). The Proxmox-level `qm resize` step correctly uses `pveFor(...)` built from the server's own node (`:94`, same `nodeFor`-style helper). The in-guest `growpart`/`resize2fs`/`xfs_growfs` step (`:199` `withServerSsh`) inherits the §1a bug. **Half-bugged**, same shape as volumes.ts: the customer's disk grows at the hypervisor but the guest filesystem never gets the news for a node-2 server.

### Game servers

**`worker/game-update.ts`** — `gameUpdateSweep()` (`:173-204`) queries `db.server.findMany` globally (no nodeId) but only enqueues `GAME_UPDATE` jobs — sweep itself is safe (pattern c). **`worker/game-control.ts`** — `gamePower`/`gameBackup` (per-job, `:101,155`) and, more importantly, **`gameScheduleSweep()`** (`:206-253`, fires every ~60s off `GameSchedule.nextRunAt`) and **`playerTrackingSweep()`** (`:266-322`, fires every ~60s, `db.server.findMany({status:"RUNNING", gamePlanId:{not:null}})` with zero nodeId scoping and not even a `node` select) — this is the single most literal match to the bug pattern you described: a genuine platform-wide sweep, on a tight cadence, whose per-server action (`withServerSsh` → RCON) inherits §1a. **Bugged**, and high-frequency (every node-2 game server's player list/session tracking and scheduled restarts are affected every minute).

### Template / OS-image "sync"

There is no template-sync job anywhere in `worker/`. `OsTemplate.vmid`/`baseVmid` (`prisma/schema.prisma:530-531`) are bare global integers with no per-node mapping. Node-2 getting a working `vmid=9000` template at all depends entirely on an admin manually running `onboard-node.sh --build-templates` (or hand-copying) on node-2 — there's no code path that verifies node-2's VMID 9000 is even the same image as node-1's, let alone keeps them in sync after either is updated. This is the (b) pattern ("a hardcoded identifier used without confirming it means the same thing on every node"), but it's a one-time setup/drift risk rather than a recurring sweep failure, so I've ranked it low below.
